info.title: Sectr API
info.description: Control plane + invocation API. The journal is the source of truth: client "live" views are SSE tails of the journal, never proxies of a running runner.

post.summary: Create a session and start its first turn
post.description: Dual auth: invocation key (end-user path, origin="api") or platform principal (dashboard playground, origin="playground"). Starts the turn immediately with `input` as a user_message reason. A user token (`sks_`, SEC-67) creates a session OWNED by its bound end user; invocation-key sessions are ownerless (backend-only).

input.description: Opaque JSON, journaled in INVOCATION_STARTED.reason.input. Not empty: a string of only whitespace, or an empty list, is a 400.

429.description: concurrency, capacity or rate limit (SEC-75; server policy — the dev gateway never returns it). Retry the same request after the `Retry-After` delay. On `/input` and `/approval` nothing was journaled. On `POST /sessions` normally nothing was either, but if a concurrent request took the last slot between admission and the first turn's claim, an idle session (only `SESSION_CREATED`) may be left behind; it is listed by `GET /sessions` and accepts `/input` later. `code` says which limit tripped (see the body schema).

get.summary: List sessions (sessions tables, approvals inbox source)

parameters.name: external_user_id
parameters.description: owner filter (backend/platform callers only; rejected for browser tokens, which are always scoped to their own user)

post.description: Server-to-server (SEC-67). The app's backend, authenticated with its invocation key, asserts the end-user identity its own auth established; the returned opaque `sks_` token is safe to hand to that user's browser. It can create sessions owned by the user, list only their sessions, and get/stream/input/decide approvals on them. Rate-limited per (key, external_user_id): 429 when exhausted. TTL 24h by default (server-configurable).

app.description: the invocation key's own app (id or slug)

201.description: minted; the token is shown once

400.description: invalid request or app does not match the key

get.summary: Journal tail (SSE) — the ONLY live view; never proxied from a runner
get.description: `text/event-stream`. Each frame's `data:` is one event envelope (event.schema.json); the SSE `id:` is the event's UUIDv7 `id`. Replays the full journal from seq 0, then holds the tail open. Resumption: standard `Last-Event-ID` header (or `last_event_id` query param for first-connect) → replay `WHERE seq > $1`.

post.description: Journaled as an INVOCATION_STARTED with reason user_message. 202 means the turn is SCHEDULED — turns run asynchronously; follow the SSE journal tail for the output. An input after an ERRORED turn is accepted (a fresh turn is the recovery path).

409.description: session not accepting input — mid-turn (a live lease holds the session), awaiting an approval decision (decide it first: a new message would strand the unanswered tool call in the conversation), or ended. NOT a 409 after an errored turn.

post.summary: Decide a pending approval (banner, approvals inbox)
post.description: Journaled as TOOL_APPROVAL_GRANTED/DENIED, then the platform resumes the turn with an approval_decision invocation.

409.description: no pending approval on this session

get.summary: Pending approvals across all apps (admin approvals inbox)

parameters.name: route
parameters.description: the manifest route path without its leading slash (`/chat` → `chat`). Nested routes keep their slashes (`/ag-ui/my-app/support/chat`), which OpenAPI path templates cannot express. Must be a route of the app's active deployment.

post.summary: Run the agent (AG-UI 1.0) — one turn, streamed
post.description: One AG-UI run is one Sectr turn: `threadId` is the session id (a UUID) and the stream is that turn's events projected to AG-UI, ending in exactly one `RUN_FINISHED` or `RUN_ERROR`. A new `threadId` creates the session, owned by a user token's end user; it must start empty (earlier history → 400). On an existing thread the client's `messages` are ignored except the trailing user message: `RUN_STARTED` is followed by a `MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT` of the journal. A tool needing approval ends the run with `RUN_FINISHED {outcome: {type: interrupt}}`; the client answers with a run carrying `resume: [{interruptId, status, payload}]` (`payload: true` approves, `false` or `status: cancelled` denies). An invalid resume is a 200 stream of `RUN_STARTED` + `RUN_ERROR` (`code: invalid_run`), not an HTTP error. CORS: any origin, `GET`/`POST`, headers `authorization, content-type, accept`; preflights are answered before auth. Platform keys are refused (403).

200.description: AG-UI event stream: one JSON event per `data:` frame, keep-alive comments every 15 s, no `id:` field (runs are not resumable; reconnect with GET instead).

400.description: malformed `RunAgentInput`; `protocolVersion` not 1.x; `threadId` not a UUID; trailing message not `role: user`, or empty (only whitespace, or no content parts); history on a new thread

get.summary: Reconnect to a thread — re-stream its latest run (read-only)
get.description: The server half of an AG-UI client's `connect()` (SEC-130; outside AG-UI 1.0, which has no reconnect). Streams the thread's latest run as a run would: `RUN_STARTED` (the original `runId`), a `MESSAGES_SNAPSHOT` of the history before it, then the run's events: replayed, then live until its terminal event. So a reloaded page gets a finished turn, a turn still streaming, or the same pending interrupt back. A thread that doesn't exist yet, or has no run, is an empty 200. Writes nothing and starts nothing; never 429. Same credentials, CORS and ownership rules as POST.

post.description: SUPERSEDED by SEC-69 (Clerk sign-in → `POST /auth/clerk`); never implemented by the server. Kept only as the historical cookie-flow sketch.

post.summary: Exchange a Clerk session JWT for a short-lived dashboard-session platform key
post.description: SEC-69: the dashboard's Clerk sign-in (GitHub / Google). The Clerk session JWT is verified networklessly (RS256 against the instance's public key; `iss`, `exp`/`nbf`, `azp`, `sub`, and the custom `email` claim). The account is resolved by the Clerk `sub` alone (no linking by email): a returning Clerk user gets their org, anyone else a brand-new org + user. Then an ordinary `platform` key with an `expires_at` (`SECTR_DASHBOARD_SESSION_TTL_SECS`, default 7 days, named `dashboard session (Clerk)`) is minted. The token goes in the BODY, never `Authorization`. The key is returned once and never logged.

created.description: this sign-in created the org (route to the Getting-started checklist)

401.description: invalid Clerk session (any verification failure; no detail on the wire)

403.description: `{"error": <message>, "code": "beta_full"}` — the signup cap is reached and no org was created (SEC-75 owns the cap). Clients branch on `code`; `error` is human-readable.

500.description: the Clerk session-token template lacks the `email` claim (operator misconfiguration)

503.description: Clerk is not configured, or a non-Postgres deployment

post.summary: Sign out — revoke the presented dashboard-session key
post.description: SEC-69. Platform principal. Revokes the PRESENTED key only if it has an `expires_at` (a dashboard-session key); a pasted long-lived key is never revoked by signing out. Any live platform key gets a 204, whether or not it was revoked. A repeat call with a key that is already revoked is a 401, as on every authenticated route.

401.description: missing, unknown, revoked or expired key

get.summary: List apps (console overview, sidebar, command palette)
App detail (overview tab — agents, deployments, URL)

post.description: Multipart upload of the packaged agent + manifest. First deploy for an unknown app name creates the app (CLI-first creation). Auth: platform API key.

202.description: Accepted — the build runs off-request. The response body is the deployment row in `building` state; poll `GET /apps/{appId}/deployments` until `status` reaches `active` or `failed` (a `failed` row carries its `error`).

400.description: Validation failure: unreadable multipart (the `tarball` or `manifest` field could not be read), or the body is missing a required field.

422.description: Validation/rejection failure: invalid `sectr.toml` (not TOML, missing or empty `agent.entry`), the app has a secret named `SECTR_APPROVAL_POLICY` (Sectr sets that variable from `[deploy] approval_tools`; remove the secret), or the deploy was rejected server-side (registry/artifact-store error — a version collision under concurrent deploys of the same app surfaces here).

post.summary: Make a deployment current (dashboard rollback / promote)
post.description: New sessions pin to the newly-active deployment; existing sessions keep their pinned deployment.

409.description: Deployment not in a ready state — only `active` or `retired` rows (a resolved build) can be activated; `building` and `failed` targets are rejected.

post.summary: Create an API key — full value returned exactly once
post.description: Mints either key class. Platform keys are org-scoped; invocation keys must carry the `app_id` they scope to (the DDL CHECK enforces the class/app_id consistency too). The full value is returned once and never stored — only its SHA-256 hash.

invocationKey.description: per-app invocation key minted in the dashboard settings — the trusted-backend / minting credential; never ship it to a browser in a multi-user app

userToken.description: short-TTL end-user browser token (`sks_`) minted via POST /tokens. Also accepted as `?token=` on the SSE endpoint only (EventSource cannot set headers) — access logs must redact it.

RunAgentInput.description: AG-UI 1.0 `RunAgentInput` (https://docs.ag-ui.com/sdk/js/core/types#runagentinput). Sectr reads the fields below; `state` and `parentRunId` are accepted and ignored, and `tools` is accepted but unused (frontend tools are not supported yet).

threadId.description: the Sectr session id; a new one creates the session

runId.description: the client's run id: echoed in RUN_STARTED and journaled (the invocation id stays server-minted)

protocolVersion.description: optional; must be 1.x (minor versions are additive)

messages.description: AG-UI messages. The trailing one must be `role: user` (its `content` becomes the turn's input), except on a resume run. On a new thread nothing but `system` / `developer` messages may precede it; on an existing thread earlier messages are ignored (the journal is the history).

resume.description: the answer to the pending approval interrupt, which makes this a resume run

forwardedProps.description: journaled with the run; not yet exposed to agent code

context.description: journaled with the run; not yet exposed to agent code

AgUiEvent.description: One AG-UI 1.0 event (https://docs.ag-ui.com/concepts/events). Every event carries `timestamp` (ms) and `metadata: {seq}` (the journal sequence number). Not emitted: `STATE_*`, `*_CHUNK`, `ACTIVITY_*`, `RUN_FINISHED.usage`.

Me.description: MVP: no user records exist (paste-a-platform-key login, decided 2026-09-12), so `user` is absent; `org` is the authenticated principal's org.

url.description: public app host (null in the MVP)

ApiKeyMeta.description: Metadata only — the store keeps SHA-256 hashes, so no display prefix exists; `name` identifies keys. `revoked_at` non-null keys authenticate as nonexistent.

expires_at.description: hard expiry (SEC-69 dashboard-session keys, minted by POST /auth/clerk); expired keys authenticate as nonexistent. Null = never expires.

EventEnvelope.title: Sectr journal event envelope
EventEnvelope.description:
Canonical event model for Sectr. Every journal row and every client SSE frame is one envelope. The envelope ties a closed `type` enum to a per-type payload schema via the `typedEvent` oneOf.

Forward compatibility: `additionalProperties` is deliberately NOT false anywhere in this schema — payload/envelope objects may carry unknown fields, and readers must preserve them, so events written by newer writers remain valid for older readers.

`seq` is a per-session monotonic integer assigned by the journal writer (the server's ingest path), gap-free within a turn, starting at 0. It is never supplied by user code. `id` is a UUIDv7 (time-ordered) minted by the platform's event producer (the engine — never user code) and deduped by the journal writer, enabling exactly-once reconnect replay; the SSE frame's `id:` field carries it, enabling `Last-Event-ID` resumption.

Runner-emitted event types may only appear on the SSE response stream of the invoke contract (see `invocation.schema.json` $defs/runnerEvent); platform-emitted types are written by the server/sidecar only.

Turn semantics: a turn starts with a user_message invocation and ends when NO_MORE_ACTIONS is journaled within it (also synthesized by the sidecar after SESSION_ERROR). An approval pause SUSPENDS the turn — TOOL_APPROVAL_REQUIRED is then the last runner event, and no NO_MORE_ACTIONS is emitted until the decision's resume invocation completes.

uuidv7.description: Lowercase UUIDv7 — version nibble 7, RFC 9562 variant.

runnerEventType.description: The subset of event types a runner (user process) may emit over the invoke response stream. Everything else is platform-emitted. The turn ends when NO_MORE_ACTIONS is emitted; an approval pause (TOOL_APPROVAL_REQUIRED last) does NOT end the turn. TRANSCRIPT_COMPACTED is emitted by the SDK/adapter when the agent framework compacts context.

typedEvent.description: Discriminated union: each branch pins `type` to a const and binds the payload to that type's schema.

MESSAGE_START.description: Runner-emitted. Start of an assistant message.

MESSAGE_DELTA.description: Runner-emitted. Content delta for a message. Deltas are INTERPRETABLE, not opaque: the platform (e.g. a future AG-UI-compatible endpoint) must be able to reconstruct both the exact transcript and its streaming semantics from the journal alone. Tool-argument streaming is deliberately NOT a delta kind — TOOL_CALL journals complete arguments, which a resumed runner executes from journal data alone.

delta.description: Interpretable content delta: {type, text} with a CLOSED kind vocabulary — `text` (maps to AG-UI TEXT_MESSAGE_CONTENT) and `reasoning` (maps to THINKING_CONTENT). One wire shape only; unknown kinds are invalid: framework chunk types outside the vocabulary must be normalized by the SDK adapter before journaling (e.g. Anthropic input_json_delta accumulates into TOOL_CALL.arguments).

MESSAGE_END.description: Runner-emitted. End of an assistant message.

framework_state.description: What the adapter that wrote it needs to rehydrate and replay THIS model response as its agent framework stored it, beyond the message's text and tool calls (e.g. signed reasoning); never state of other responses or of the run as a whole. Its `data` is opaque to the platform, which stores and serves it but never interprets it; only the adapter named by `adapter` reads it back. At most 256 KiB serialized: the platform drops a larger one.

adapter.description: The adapter that wrote it, e.g. "langgraph".

data.description: The adapter's own data, in its format `v`. Opaque to the platform. The journal keeps a string value exactly, byte for byte, but an object or a number only by value: an object's keys may come back in another order, and a number in another notation. So a value the adapter needs back exactly (e.g. text a provider gets verbatim) is stored as a string; structure it only reads may be stored as JSON.

TOOL_CALL.description: Runner-emitted. Journal record of a tool call initiated inside the runner — the platform NEVER executes tools. Arguments are opaque JSON (conventionally an object) journaled verbatim; name + arguments must be sufficient for a resumed runner to execute an approved call from journal data alone.

TOOL_APPROVAL_REQUIRED.description: Runner-emitted. Requests human approval for a tool call. MUST be the final runner event of a turn; the turn ends with TURN_END{stop_reason: "awaiting_approval"}.

reason.description: Human-readable explanation shown in the approval inbox.

ERROR.description: Runner-emitted. Runner-level error; ends the turn (followed by TURN_END{stop_reason: "error"}).

transient.description: True if a retry of the same invocation may succeed.

SESSION_CREATED.description: Platform-emitted (seq 0 of a session). Optional `external_user_id` (SEC-67): the session's owner when created via a user-scope browser token — the app-defined end-user identity; absent for backend/platform-created sessions.

external_user_id.description: owner identity: the (app-scoped) end-user the session belongs to; absent when backend/platform-created

INVOCATION_STARTED.description: Platform-emitted. One per invocation, appended BEFORE the sidecar fetches the transcript — so the runner's transcript already includes its own INVOCATION_STARTED, and the canonical messages view already contains the current user message. `reason` says why this invocation exists.

TOOL_RESULT.description: Runner-emitted. Journaled after every SUCCESSFUL tool execution — normal mid-turn calls and post-approval executions alike — and for a denied approval (the rejection text). A model conversation needs an output for every function_call, but the journal does not guarantee one: every prefix of a valid journal is itself valid (a crash can cut it anywhere, including between TOOL_CALL and TOOL_RESULT), and a tool that fails journals no TOOL_RESULT (failure semantics: SEC-123). The canonical fold supplies the missing output: a TOOL_CALL with no TOOL_RESULT that is followed by more conversation gets a synthesized, never-persisted tool output; a trailing one is a suspended approval. The approval decision itself is journaled by the platform as TOOL_APPROVAL_GRANTED/DENIED.

TOOL_APPROVAL_GRANTED.description: Platform-emitted. The approval decision itself, journaled.

TOOL_APPROVAL_DENIED.description: Platform-emitted. The approval decision itself, journaled.

SESSION_ERROR.description: Platform-emitted. Platform-level failure (runner crash, timeout, lease expiry).

envelope.description: Alias reference to this schema's root envelope, for cross-file $refs (e.g. invocation.schema.json transcripts).

runnerEvent.description: One frame of the runner's SSE response stream in the invoke contract: `{type, payload}` only — `id`, `seq`, `session_id`, `deployment_id` and `created_at` are assigned by the journal writer (the server's ingest path) when the event is journaled. Restricted to runner-emitted types.

transcript.description: Full session history as journal envelopes, rehydrated by the platform and passed to the runner in the invoke request.

NO_MORE_ACTIONS.description: Runner-emitted (synthesized by the SDK driver on generator exhaustion or after an unhandled error's ERROR event; synthesized by the sidecar after SESSION_ERROR on a runner crash). THE turn-ending sentinel: 'the agent has no pending actions — the ball is in the user's court.' Deliberately NOT emitted on an approval pause: a gated tool is a pending action, so the turn is suspended, not over. Raw (no-SDK) runners MUST end their stream with this event when the turn is complete.

invocationReason.description: Why an invocation exists. `tool_result` kind is specified for post-MVP externally-executed tools (the platform never executes tools in MVP).

input.description: The user's message — opaque JSON, exactly as submitted. Starts a turn (first or follow-up).

TRANSCRIPT_COMPACTED.description: Runner-emitted when the agent framework compacts context (framework's algorithm, framework's model access — the SDK/adapter captures the result and journals it mid-stream). Payload is the FULL post-compaction context in canonical message form: context assembly = these messages + the canonical view of everything journaled after this event (positional fold; `replaces_up_to_seq` is metadata — the journal head at compaction time). Constraint: the snapshot must not drop an unanswered tool call (an open function_call without its output is an invalid context on replay).

messages.description: OpenAI-style message dicts (the canonical view) — the entire new context, framework compaction output normalized.

ErrorWithCode.description: The standard `{error}` body, plus an optional machine-readable `code` on errors that have one (additive: existing errors carry no code).

code.description: `concurrency_limit` (the app's concurrent-turn cap), `platform_capacity` (the platform-wide cap), `rate_limited` (session-creation rate limit), `beta_full` (signup cap; 403 on POST /alpha/provision).

route.description: the agent this session talked to

external_user_id.description: owner (SEC-67) — the end user whose browser token created the session; absent for backend/platform-created sessions

input.description: Opaque JSON, journaled in INVOCATION_STARTED.reason.input. Not empty: a string of only whitespace, or an empty list, is a 400.
Opaque JSON, journaled in INVOCATION_STARTED.reason.input. Not empty: a string of only whitespace, or an empty list, is a 400.

TooManyRequests.description: concurrency, capacity or rate limit (SEC-75; server policy — the dev gateway never returns it). Retry the same request after the `Retry-After` delay. On `/input` and `/approval` nothing was journaled. On `POST /sessions` normally nothing was either, but if a concurrent request took the last slot between admission and the first turn's claim, an idle session (only `SESSION_CREATED`) may be left behind; it is listed by `GET /sessions` and accepts `/input` later. `code` says which limit tripped (see the body schema).

EmptyInput.description: `input` is empty: a string of only whitespace (or no characters), or an empty list. Nothing is journaled; some framework and provider pairs can't send an empty user message.
